At that concentration of Cl2, the concentration of Ag1 has been reduced to 3.3 3 1029 from the original concentration of 0.10 m. In other words, only about three Ag1 ions in 108 remain in solution, but all the Pb21 ions are left in solution. A nearly perfect separation of the two ionic species has been achieved.

This calculation gave the optimal theoretical separation factor for the two ions. In practice it is necessary to keep the chloride concentration lower. If [Cl2] is ten times smaller, or 0.0049 m, about three Ag1 ions in 107 remain in solution with the Pb21. This is ten times more Ag1 than if [Cl2] 5 0.049 m, but the separation of Ag1 from Pb21 is still very good.
